claims.text: Machine-learning-guided selection of SPS parameters will reduce the required sintering temperature for powder-based ceramic or metal systems.
Machine-learning-guided SPS will limit grain growth.
A machine learning model can use historical experimental data to predict and fine-tune SPS heating rate, pressure, dwell time, and sintering additives.
Reduced thermal exposure produces refined grain boundaries and controlled grain size.
The machine learning model identifies non-obvious interactions among SPS parameters.
Identification and optimization of interactions among SPS parameters lowers the activation energy for densification.
Lower activation energy enables effective densification at lower temperatures.
The proposed method will reduce sintering temperature by 10–20% relative to conventional SPS.
The proposed method will maintain or improve densification despite the lower sintering temperature.
The proposed method will restrict grain growth relative to conventional SPS.
The approach is expected to be effective for material systems having ample prior experimental data.
The effectiveness of the approach for systems lacking ample prior experimental data is uncertain.
The achievable temperature reduction and microstructural properties depend on the quality and breadth of the historical dataset.
The method may not generalize across all materials.
